sections.h2: Fastest ways to sell in Johnson City
sections.html:
Speed favors a cash buyer who takes the house as is, because that route skips lender approval, an appraisal and rounds of repair talks. A traditional listing suits an owner with no deadline who wants the widest range of buyers.

The city has a university, a big hospital sector and a large rental market, so one house might appeal to an owner-occupant, a landlord or a renovator. That mix is useful when yours needs work.

  • Hire an agent if the house shows well and you can wait for financing to clear.
  • Sell directly if you already have a buyer and only need a closing agent.
  • Take a cash offer for a firm date or to avoid paying for repairs.

sections.h2: About the city and its school zones
sections.html:
Johnson City lies in an Appalachian valley, mostly in Washington County with pieces in Carter and Sullivan counties. Medicine and education carry the local economy. East Tennessee State University enrolls about 16,000 students, and Ballad Health, the region's largest health system, is based here. Johnson City Medical Center has a Level 1 trauma center and Niswonger Children's Hospital.

Most addresses fall in the Johnson City Independent School District, home to Science Hill High School, Indian Trail Middle and Liberty Bell Middle. Small parts of the city belong to the Washington County district, so confirm the district for your street before you advertise a school zone.

The city had 74,943 residents on July 1, 2025, up 5.5 percent from April 2020, with 30,662 households.

  • Typical value of an owner's home: $268,200
  • Homes lived in by owners: 51.3 percent
  • Middle gross rent: $1,023
  • Middle household income: $57,254
  • Average trip to work: 18.7 minutes

About half of homes are rented and a university sits in the middle of town, so landlords belong in your buyer pool. Duplexes and houses near campus can draw extra interest. Johnson City Transit runs 11 fixed routes and logged 386,917 trips in 2025, which is worth mentioning in a description along with commute time.

The city collects its own tax, and the Washington County Trustee collects the county's. For 2026, the city balance is due February 28, 2027, with penalty and interest starting March 1, 2027.

Pay the city at the Municipal and Safety Building, 601 E. Main Street, between 8 and 5 on weekdays, mail a check to P.O. Box 2227, or pay online and absorb a 2.75 percent charge. The tax office answers at 423-434-6299.

The county rate for 2023 was $2.15 per $100 of assessed value, and city residents pay more on top of that. State law fixes the tax roll as of January 1, and closings normally prorate the bill and make the buyer responsible afterward.

sections.h2: Where a Johnson City deed is filed
sections.html:
Most parcels belong to the Washington County Register of Deeds in the historic courthouse at 100 E. Main Street, Jonesborough, phone 423-753-1644. Hours run from 8 to 4:30 on weekdays, but no new recordings are taken after 4 p.m. The office collects the state's transfer and mortgage taxes along with filing charges. The transfer rate is $0.37 per $100 of price.

Washington County also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that emails you when something is filed under your name. The city spills into Sullivan and Carter counties, so check your tax bill or call the register to learn which county holds your parcel before you plan a closing.

Johnson City's Building Division issues most construction permits through its CityView portal or at the counter in City Hall. A single-family owner who lives in the house may act as general contractor and may do electrical or plumbing work after passing a free competency exam. Gas-fired mechanical work must go to a mechanical contractor with a state license. Questions and inspection requests go to 423-434-6047.

Short stays are taxed. Every stay under 30 days, however booked, carries the city's 7 percent Hotel/Motel Transient Occupancy Privilege Tax, and continuous stays of 90 days or longer are exempt. Operators also collect state and local sales tax, so the total changes with the county: 16.5 percent in the Washington County part, 16.25 percent in the Sullivan County part and 16.75 percent in the Carter County part. The finance department's tax specialist is at 423-232-1480.

sections.h2: Repairs and inspections before you list
sections.html:
The city publishes a guide to common residential inspection failures, a handy checklist before you list. Under the 2012 International Residential Code as the city cites it, a deck skips permitting only if it is no more than 200 square feet, no higher than 30 inches above grade, detached from the house and not serving a required exit. Prefabricated pools less than 24 inches deep are also exempt.

Additions, attached decks and covered porches require a site drawing and a permit. Inspection requests received by 4:30 p.m. may be scheduled for the next business day. A cash buyer may take a house with open items, while a buyer with a loan may want them resolved first.

Before you accept an offer, gather your tax bills, your loan payoff and permit papers for work done on the house. Title work then confirms the parcel's county, the tax proration and the deed. A cash purchase leaves out lender approval and an appraisal, so those two steps cannot hold up the closing date. Whichever route you choose, call the register early if any part of your parcel sits in Sullivan or Carter County.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 property tax deadline in Johnson City?
faqs.a: February 28, 2027. Penalty and interest begin March 1, 2027. The tax office is 423-434-6299.

faqs.q: Where is a Johnson City deed recorded?
faqs.a: Parcels in Washington County go to the Register of Deeds at 100 E. Main Street, Jonesborough, 423-753-1644, which takes no recordings after 4 p.m. Parcels in the Sullivan or Carter County parts fall under those counties' registers.

faqs.q: Can I act as my own contractor in Johnson City?
faqs.a: If you own and live in a single-family home, yes. Doing your own electrical or plumbing also requires passing a free competency exam, and mechanical work must go to a contractor with a state license.

faqs.q: Which tax applies to short-term rentals in Johnson City?
faqs.a: Stays under 30 days owe the city's 7 percent occupancy tax plus state and local sales tax. The total is 16.5 percent in the Washington County portion.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Johnson City sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is $0.37 per $100 of price. The sales contract decides whether the buyer or the seller pays it.
